contents.html: 4.5.1 GeMSS
contents.html_ja: 4.5.1 GeMSS
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。p.57 を描画して照合。見出し。

contents.html: GeMSS (a Great Multivariate Short Signature) is a signature scheme that follows the hash-and-sign paradigm with the application of Feistel–Patarin iterations. GeMSS uses a trapdoor function based on Hidden Field Equation with Vinegar variables and the Minus modifier (HFEv-).
contents.html_ja: GeMSS（a Great Multivariate Short Signature）は、hash-and-sign パラダイムに従い、Feistel–Patarin 反復を適用する署名方式です。GeMSS は、Vinegar 変数と Minus 修飾子を伴う隠れ体方程式（HFEv-）に基づくトラップドア関数を使用します。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。p.57 を描画して照合。

contents.html: Design. GeMSS belongs to the big field family of multivariate cryptosystems. The basic idea of these schemes is to use a bijective mapping between \(GF(q^n)\) and \(GF(q)^n\) so that the multivariate trapdoor function (expressed in terms of the small field \(GF(q)\)) can be re-expressed as a univariate function over the big field, \(GF(q^n)\). So expressed, the function can be efficiently inverted. To produce a public key, the function is composed with linear maps over the small field, which is presumed to hide the structure. The HFE cryptosystem [257] was introduced after the original big field scheme of Matsumoto and Imai [258] was broken by [259]. However, HFE with secure parameters has very slow signing. The Vinegar and Minus modifier were added by [260] in an effort to increase security at little cost in performance.
contents.html_ja: 設計。GeMSS は、多変数暗号システムの大きな体の族に属します。これらの方式の基本的な考え方は、\(GF(q^n)\) と \(GF(q)^n\) の間の全単射写像を用いて、（小さな体 \(GF(q)\) で表現された）多変数のトラップドア関数を、大きな体 \(GF(q^n)\) 上の一変数関数として表現し直せるようにすることです。そのように表現すると、この関数は効率的に逆算できます。公開鍵を生成するため、この関数は小さな体上の線形写像と合成され、これにより構造が隠蔽されると想定されています。HFE 暗号システム [257] は、Matsumoto と Imai による元の大きな体の方式 [258] が [259] により破られた後に導入されました。しかし、安全なパラメータの HFE は署名が非常に遅くなります。Vinegar と Minus 修飾子は、性能をほとんど犠牲にせずに安全性を高める試みとして、[260] により追加されました。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。p.57 を描画して照合。数式を LaTeX にする。

contents.html: Security. The security of GeMSS depends on multiple assumptions. It is assumed that, on average, instances of GeMSS produce hard instances of the \(\mathcal{MQ}\) problem in, the context of directly inverting the public key, and of the MinRank problem (see Section 3.2.2).
contents.html_ja: 安全性。GeMSS の安全性は、複数の仮定に依存します。平均的には、GeMSS のインスタンスが、公開鍵を直接逆算する文脈での \(\mathcal{MQ}\) 問題と、MinRank 問題（3.2.2 節を参照）の困難なインスタンスを生成すると仮定されています。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。p.57 を描画して照合。p.58 冒頭まで続く段落。「problem in, the context」のカンマは原本どおり。

contents.html: Performance. Like most other multivariate schemes, GeMSS produces small signatures but has a very large public key (see Table 9). Compared to Rainbow, the submitted parameters for GeMSS yield slightly smaller signatures, but the public key is significantly larger, and the signing and key generation operations are significantly slower. GeMSS defines six sets of parameters: GeMSS, BlueGeMSS, RedGeMSS, WhiteGeMSS, CyanGeMSS and MagentaGeMSS. The WhiteGeMSS, CyanGeMSS and MagentaGeMSS parameter sets were added in the third round and use fewer rounds in the Feistel-Patarin construction than the GeMSS, BlueGeMSS and RedGeMSS parameter sets. GeMSS and WhiteGeMSS rely the least (although still significantly) on the vinegar and minus modifiers for their security. These parameter sets have the slowest signing algorithms as a result. RedGeMSS and MagentaGeMSS rely the most on the vinegar and minus modifiers and are the fastest. BlueGeMSS and CyanGeMSS are intermediate.
contents.html_ja: 性能。他のほとんどの多変数方式と同様に、GeMSS は小さな署名を生成しますが、公開鍵は非常に大きくなります（表 9 を参照）。Rainbow と比べると、提出された GeMSS のパラメータは署名がわずかに小さくなりますが、公開鍵ははるかに大きく、署名と鍵生成の操作ははるかに遅くなります。GeMSS は 6 つのパラメータセット、すなわち GeMSS、BlueGeMSS、RedGeMSS、WhiteGeMSS、CyanGeMSS、MagentaGeMSS を定義しています。WhiteGeMSS、CyanGeMSS、MagentaGeMSS のパラメータセットは第 3 ラウンドで追加されたもので、GeMSS、BlueGeMSS、RedGeMSS のパラメータセットより、Feistel-Patarin 構成のラウンド数が少なくなっています。GeMSS と WhiteGeMSS は、安全性を vinegar と minus の修飾子に依存する度合いが（それでもかなりありますが）最も低くなります。その結果、これらのパラメータセットは署名アルゴリズムが最も遅くなります。RedGeMSS と MagentaGeMSS は vinegar と minus の修飾子への依存度が最も高く、最も高速です。BlueGeMSS と CyanGeMSS はその中間です。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。p.58 を描画して照合。

contents.html: Significant events since Round 2. In Round 3, GeMSS suffered a catastrophic key-recovery attack (see [12, 109]). The attack introduces a new MinRank instance whose resolution reveals the structure of the private key. While previous MinRank attacks on HFE schemes model MinRank in essentially the same way (see [261–263]), they are all exponential in the number of vinegar variables and the number of removed equations. In contrast, the attack of [109] is polynomial in the number of vinegar variables and is not affected greatly by the number of removed equations. This attack is further improved by the techniques in [264], where it is shown how to implement the much more efficient support minors MinRank approach [144] in the case that the solution is in an extension field.
contents.html_ja: 第 2 ラウンド以降の重要な出来事。第 3 ラウンドで、GeMSS は壊滅的な鍵復元攻撃を受けました（[12, 109] を参照）。この攻撃は新しい MinRank インスタンスを導入し、その解が秘密鍵の構造を明らかにします。HFE 方式に対する従来の MinRank 攻撃は MinRank を本質的に同じ方法でモデル化していました（[261–263] を参照）が、いずれも vinegar 変数の数と除去された方程式の数に関して指数時間でした。対照的に、[109] の攻撃は vinegar 変数の数について多項式時間であり、除去された方程式の数による影響をあまり受けません。この攻撃は、[264] の手法によってさらに改良されており、解が拡大体にある場合に、はるかに効率的なサポートマイナー MinRank アプローチ [144] を実装する方法が示されています。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。p.58 を描画して照合。

contents.html: Overall Assessment. This cryptanalysis effectively establishes that the vinegar and minus modifiers fail to provide any substantial security benefit in an HFEv- construction. The result undermines the basic design principles of HFEv-. Possible modifications to repair the scheme – such as abandoning the vinegar and minus modifiers and increasing the degree of the HFE polynomial to reach the target security level or adding a projection or plus modifier to thwart the new attacks, as suggested in [265] – would both represent too large a change to the original submission and render the performance of the resulting scheme unacceptable, as shown in [264]. Therefore, NIST decided not to advance GeMSS.
contents.html_ja: 総合評価。この暗号解読は、vinegar と minus の修飾子が HFEv- 構成において実質的な安全性上の利点を何ら提供しないことを、事実上確立しています。この結果は、HFEv- の基本的な設計原理を損なうものです。方式を修復するための修正案、たとえば [265] で示唆されているように、vinegar と minus の修飾子を放棄して目標の安全性レベルに達するよう HFE 多項式の次数を上げること、あるいは新たな攻撃を阻止するために射影修飾子または plus 修飾子を追加することは、いずれも元の提出物に対する変更が大きすぎ、[264] で示されているように、結果として得られる方式の性能を許容できないものにするでしょう。したがって、NIST は GeMSS を進めないことを決定しました。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。p.58 を描画して照合。

contents.html: 4.5.2 Picnic
contents.html_ja: 4.5.2 Picnic
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。p.58 を描画して照合。見出し。

contents.html: A Picnic signature is a non-interactive zero-knowledge proof of knowledge of a secret key bound to the message being signed. Picnic was an alternate signature scheme during the third round.
contents.html_ja: Picnic の署名は、署名対象のメッセージに束縛された秘密鍵の知識の、非対話的ゼロ知識証明です。Picnic は第 3 ラウンドでは代替の署名方式でした。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。p.58 を描画して照合。

contents.html: Design. Picnic uses a symmetric block cipher called LowMC. A circuit \(C\) takes as input a plaintext block \(p\) and a secret key \(sk\), and outputs \(\mathrm{LowMC}(sk, p)\). A randomly chosen plaintext block \(p\) serves as a public key. LowMC was designed so as to allow an XOR-AND circuit with fewer AND gates than other ciphers such as AES. The “number of AND gates required” metric is called multiplicative complexity [266]. Zero-knowledge proofs of knowledge of the input to an AND-XOR circuit, given its output, are of length proportional to the number of AND gates of the circuit. AES can be computed with 32 AND gates per S-box [267] (it is not known if it can be done with fewer AND gates). This results in over 5000 AND gates in AES-128. A comparable LowMC parametrization uses under 1000 AND gates [268].
contents.html_ja: 設計。Picnic は、LowMC と呼ばれる共通鍵ブロック暗号を使用します。回路 \(C\) は、平文ブロック \(p\) と秘密鍵 \(sk\) を入力として受け取り、\(\mathrm{LowMC}(sk, p)\) を出力します。ランダムに選ばれた平文ブロック \(p\) が公開鍵として機能します。LowMC は、AES など他の暗号より AND ゲートの少ない XOR-AND 回路を可能にするよう設計されました。「必要な AND ゲート数」という指標は乗法的複雑度（multiplicative complexity）と呼ばれます [266]。AND-XOR 回路の出力が与えられたときの、その入力の知識のゼロ知識証明は、回路の AND ゲート数に比例した長さになります。AES は S-box あたり 32 個の AND ゲートで計算できます [267]（それより少ない AND ゲートでできるかどうかは知られていません）。これにより、AES-128 には 5000 を超える AND ゲートが必要になります。同等の LowMC のパラメータ化では、1000 個未満の AND ゲートを使用します [268]。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。p.58 を描画して照合。段落 3 つに分ける。XOR-AND は行末の実際のハイフン。

contents.html_ja: Picnic の署名は、秘密鍵の知識の非対話的ゼロ知識証明です。署名対象のメッセージは、秘密鍵の保持者だけがその証明を生成できるように、（ハッシュを介して）知識証明のチャレンジに組み込まれます。署名の長さは、暗号方式の乗法的複雑度と、安全なマルチパーティ計算の分野からゼロ知識知識証明を構成する MPCitH（multi-party computation in the head）手法に依存します（[269] を参照）。
contents.html: A Picnic signature is a non-interactive zero-knowledge proof of knowledge of the secret key. The message being signed is incorporated (via hashing) into the challenges of the proof of knowledge in such a way that only the holder of the secret key can produce the proof. The length of the signature depends on the multiplicative complexity of the encryption scheme and the MPCitH (multi-party computation in the head) technique to construct a zero-knowledge proof of knowledge from the field of secure multi-party computation (see [269]).
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。p.58 を描画して照合。段落 3 つに分ける。XOR-AND は行末の実際のハイフン。

contents.html_ja: Picnic は高度にモジュール化された設計です。暗号プリミティブ、すなわちハッシュ関数とブロック暗号は、さまざまな方法で具体化できます。LowMC は AES ほど研究されておらず、NIST が標準化するには、はるかに多くの分析が必要です。しかし、Picnic の基礎となるブロック暗号に対する安全性要件は、ブロック暗号の一般的な安全性要件よりはるかに緩やかです。明らかにされるのは平文と暗号文の組が 1 つだけであり、攻撃者が Picnic 署名を偽造するには、その平文をその暗号文に写す鍵を見つける必要があるためです。
contents.html: Picnic is a highly modular design. The cryptographic primitives – a hash function and block cipher – could be instantiated in different ways. LowMC has not been studied as much as AES and hence needs much more analysis before it can be standardized by NIST. However, the security requirements for the underlying block cipher in Picnic are much less stringent than the general security requirements of a block cipher, as only a single plaintext/ciphertext pair is ever revealed, and an attacker needs to find a key that maps that plaintext to that ciphertext in order to forge Picnic signatures.
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。p.58 を描画して照合。段落 3 つに分ける。XOR-AND は行末の実際のハイフン。

contents.html: Security. Picnic uses no number-theoretic or structured hardness assumptions. Its security depends on the underlying hash function behaving as a random oracle (a common cryptographic assumption) and on the security of the LowMC block cipher [268] against an adversary given a single plaintext/ciphertext pair. The security of LowMC has not been as extensively studied as that of older symmetric-key ciphers, although recent attempts to analyze LowMC’s security have found weaknesses [270–275].
contents.html_ja: 安全性。Picnic は、整数論的な、あるいは構造化された困難性の仮定を一切使用しません。その安全性は、基礎となるハッシュ関数がランダムオラクルとして振る舞うこと（一般的な暗号学的仮定）と、平文と暗号文の組が 1 つ与えられた敵対者に対する LowMC ブロック暗号 [268] の安全性に依存します。LowMC の安全性は、古くからある共通鍵暗号ほど広範に研究されていませんが、LowMC の安全性を分析する最近の試みでは、弱点が見つかっています [270–275]。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。p.59 を描画して照合。段落ごとに分ける。

contents.html_ja: 他の候補と同様に、Picnic の素直な実装には、サイドチャネルに関する重大な問題があります（[97, 276] を参照）。
contents.html: As with other candidates, a straightforward implementation of Picnic would have significant side-channel issues (see [97, 276]).
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。p.59 を描画して照合。段落ごとに分ける。

contents.html: Performance. Picnic has a small public key size and relatively large signatures. Signing speed is much faster than SPHINCS<sup>+</sup>, and verification is somewhat slower.
contents.html_ja: 性能。Picnic は、公開鍵のサイズが小さく、署名は比較的大きくなります。署名の速度は SPHINCS<sup>+</sup> よりはるかに速く、検証はやや遅くなります。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。p.59 を描画して照合。

contents.html: Significant events since Round 2. As noted in the Security section above, there were several papers which cryptanalyzed LowMC [270–275].
contents.html_ja: 第 2 ラウンド以降の重要な出来事。上の安全性の項で述べたとおり、LowMC を暗号解読した論文がいくつかありました [270–275]。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。p.59 を描画して照合。段落 3 つに分ける。3 つ目は p.60 冒頭まで続く。

contents.html_ja: AES に基づく Picnic の変種が提案されています [277]。署名方式 Banquet [278] は AES を使用し、Picnic に近い性能を達成します。Picnic と同じパラダイムの下でさらなる改良を得ることは、活発な研究分野であり（たとえば [279, 280] を参照）、最終的には、現行の設計より大幅に性能の良い署名方式につながる可能性があります。
contents.html: Variants of Picnic based on AES have been proposed [277]. The signature scheme Banquet [278] uses AES and achieves performance close to that of Picnic. Obtaining further improvements under the same paradigm as Picnic is an active area of research (see, for example, [279, 280]) and may eventually lead to a signature scheme with significantly better performance than the current design.
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。p.59 を描画して照合。段落 3 つに分ける。3 つ目は p.60 冒頭まで続く。

contents.html_ja: 総合評価。Picnic と SPHINCS<sup>+</sup> は、主として共通鍵プリミティブの安全性に依拠する、2 つの署名方式の候補でした。NIST が SPHINCS<sup>+</sup> を選んだのは、主に、LowMC の安全性を自信を持って定量化できなかったこと（たとえば [271–273] を参照）と、MPC-in-the-head パラダイムから発展する将来の暗号システムが、最終的に第 3 ラウンドの Picnic の設計を大幅に上回ると判明する可能性があることによります。
contents.html: Overall assessment. Picnic and SPHINCS<sup>+</sup> were the two candidate signature schemes that relied mostly on the security of symmetric primitives. NIST chose SPHINCS<sup>+</sup> largely because it could not confidently quantify the security of LowMC (see, for example, [271–273]) and because future cryptosystems that evolve out of the multi-party-computation-in-the-head paradigm may eventually prove significantly superior to the third-round Picnic design.
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。p.59 を描画して照合。段落 3 つに分ける。3 つ目は p.60 冒頭まで続く。

contents.html: 4.5.3 Rainbow
contents.html_ja: 4.5.3 Rainbow
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。p.60 を描画して照合。見出し。

contents.html: Rainbow is a multivariate signature scheme using the hash-and-sign paradigm with the modification of [281]. Rainbow is a layered generalization of the unbalanced oil-vinegar (UOV) scheme.
contents.html_ja: Rainbow は、[281] の修正を加えた hash-and-sign パラダイムを用いる多変数署名方式です。Rainbow は、不均衡 oil-vinegar（UOV）方式を階層化して一般化したものです。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。p.60 を描画して照合。

contents.html: Design. Rainbow belongs to the small field family of multivariate cryptosystems and to the lineage of oil-vinegar schemes such as UOV (see [282]). UOV schemes use two types of variables – oil variables and vinegar variables – to generate a multivariate quadratic map for which preimages are easily computed. Specifically, this map contains terms that are quadratic in the vinegar variables and terms that are bilinear in the oil and vinegar variables but contains no terms that are quadratic in exclusively the oil variables. In this way, the owner of the private key can randomly assign values to the vinegar variables and solve linearly for values of the oil variables.
contents.html_ja: 設計。Rainbow は、多変数暗号システムの小さな体の族に属し、UOV（[282] を参照）のような oil-vinegar 方式の系譜にあります。UOV 方式は、oil 変数と vinegar 変数という 2 種類の変数を使用して、原像を容易に計算できる多変数二次写像を生成します。具体的には、この写像は、vinegar 変数について二次の項と、oil 変数と vinegar 変数について双線形の項を含みますが、oil 変数のみについて二次の項は含みません。このようにして、秘密鍵の所有者は、vinegar 変数にランダムに値を割り当て、oil 変数の値を線形に解くことができます。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。p.60 を描画して照合。段落ごとに分ける。

contents.html_ja: Rainbow は、この基本的な構成を、異なる oil 変数の集合を持つ層を定義することで一般化しており、これらの層は、層ごとに順次解くことができます（[283] を参照）。その後、構造を隠すために、写像全体が線形写像と合成されます。Rainbow の構成で層を用いることで、追加の構造を持つ代償として、従来の UOV よりも署名が小さく、検証が高速になります。
contents.html: Rainbow generalizes this basic construction by defining layers with differing sets of oil variables that can be sequentially solved, layer by layer (see [283]). The entire map is then composed with linear maps to hide the structure. The use of layers in the Rainbow construction allows smaller signatures and faster verification than traditional UOV at the cost of extra structure.
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。p.60 を描画して照合。段落ごとに分ける。

contents.html: Security. Rainbow’s security depends on several hardness assumptions. It is assumed that, on average, instances of Rainbow produce hard instances of several problems including the \(\mathcal{MQ}\) problem, in the context of directly inverting the public key, and the MinRank problem (see subsection 3.2.2).
contents.html_ja: 安全性。Rainbow の安全性は、いくつかの困難性の仮定に依存します。平均的には、Rainbow のインスタンスが、公開鍵を直接逆算する文脈での \(\mathcal{MQ}\) 問題や、MinRank 問題（3.2.2 節を参照）を含む、いくつかの問題の困難なインスタンスを生成すると仮定されています。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。p.60 を描画して照合。

contents.html: Performance. Rainbow has efficient signing and verification, and produces very short signatures. Rainbow key generation, however, is significantly slower than signing or verifying. Still, key generation is comparable to that of FALCON. The key sizes of Rainbow parameters are quite large in comparison to other finalists but are still significantly smaller than GeMSS (see Tables 8 and 9).
contents.html_ja: 性能。Rainbow は署名と検証が効率的で、非常に短い署名を生成します。ただし、Rainbow の鍵生成は、署名や検証よりも大幅に遅くなります。それでも、鍵生成は FALCON と同程度です。Rainbow のパラメータの鍵サイズは、他のファイナリストと比べるとかなり大きいものの、GeMSS よりは大幅に小さくなります（表 8 と表 9 を参照）。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。p.60 を描画して照合。

contents.html: Significant events since Round 2. Parameters were updated between Round 2 and Round 3 due to updated analysis in [284] showing that the second round parameters of Rainbow were very slightly below the NIST security categories. A new method of generating a MinRank problem from the Rainbow public key was discovered in [11]. Together with the support minors method of solving MinRank instances (see [144]), this new “rectangular MinRank attack” reduced the complexity of the best known attacks on the various Rainbow parameter sets by 20 to 55 bits of security in the gate metric, showing that all of the Rainbow parameter sets fall significantly below their security targets, when memory costs are ignored. Subsequently, an analysis incorporating the significant memory access cost of this attack [264] suggests that all of the Rainbow parameters fail to meet their purported security levels, even when memory costs are taken into account. Finally, a new attack [13] provides a new hybrid combinatorial/algebraic attack and an improvement of the rectangular MinRank attacks that further reduces the security of all parameter sets to the extent that an attack on Rainbow-I has become practical.
contents.html_ja: 第 2 ラウンド以降の重要な出来事。第 2 ラウンドの Rainbow のパラメータが NIST の安全性カテゴリをわずかに下回っていたことを示す [284] の更新分析により、第 2 ラウンドと第 3 ラウンドの間にパラメータが更新されました。Rainbow の公開鍵から MinRank 問題を生成する新しい方法が [11] で発見されました。MinRank インスタンスを解くサポートマイナー法（[144] を参照）と合わせて、この新しい「長方形 MinRank 攻撃」は、メモリコストを無視した場合、ゲート数を指標とした既知最良の攻撃の計算量を、Rainbow の各パラメータセットについて安全性ビットで 20～55 ビット低下させ、すべてのパラメータセットが安全性目標を大幅に下回ることを示しました。その後、この攻撃に伴う大きなメモリアクセスコストを織り込んだ分析 [264] は、メモリコストを考慮しても Rainbow のすべてのパラメータが主張されている安全性レベルを満たさないことを示唆しています。最後に、新しい攻撃 [13] は、新たな組合せ的・代数的ハイブリッド攻撃を提示するとともに長方形 MinRank 攻撃を改良し、すべてのパラメータセットの安全性をさらに低下させ、Rainbow-I への攻撃が実用的になるほどにしました。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。p.60 を描画して照合。p.61 冒頭まで続く段落。

contents.html: Overall assessment. The best known attacks of Rainbow have significantly affected the security of the scheme. In fact, in light of the new attacks, it is not clear that secure instantiations of Rainbow can offer any performance advantage in comparison to the less structured UOV scheme without significant re-engineering. Therefore, NIST decided not to advance Rainbow.
contents.html_ja: 総合評価。Rainbow に対する既知の最良の攻撃は、方式の安全性に大きな影響を与えました。実際、新たな攻撃を踏まえると、大幅な再設計なしには、Rainbow の安全な具体化が、構造の少ない UOV 方式に比べて何らかの性能上の利点を提供できるかどうかは明らかではありません。したがって、NIST は Rainbow を進めないことを決定しました。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。p.61 を描画して照合。

contents.html: 5. Conclusion
contents.html_ja: 5. 結論
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。p.61 を描画して照合。章見出し。

contents.html: NIST greatly appreciates the participation in the NIST PQC Standardization Process. It has been a long and complex process so far. Six years have passed since NIST issued its Call for Proposals for PQC algorithms, and there have been significant efforts from submitters, researchers, implementers, industry, and the cryptographic community. With the conclusion of the third round, NIST is pleased to announce the first public-key algorithms that will provide protection from quantum attacks to be standardized.
contents.html_ja: NIST は、NIST PQC 標準化プロセスへの参加に深く感謝します。これまでのところ、長く複雑なプロセスでした。NIST が PQC アルゴリズムの提案募集を発行してから 6 年が経ち、提出者、研究者、実装者、産業界、暗号コミュニティによる多大な努力がありました。第 3 ラウンドの終了にあたり、NIST は、量子攻撃からの保護を提供する、標準化される最初の公開鍵アルゴリズムを発表できることを喜ばしく思います。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。p.61 を描画して照合。段落ごとに分ける。

contents.html_ja: NIST が大半のユースケースに推奨する主たるアルゴリズムは、CRYSTALS–KYBER（鍵確立）と CRYSTALS–Dilithium（デジタル署名）です。加えて、署名方式の FALCON と SPHINCS<sup>+</sup> も標準化されます。候補の BIKE、Classic McEliece、HQC、SIKE は、すべて第 4 ラウンドの評価でさらなる研究のために継続されます。これらの選択の理由は、本報告書の前半で示しました。
contents.html: The primary algorithms NIST recommends for most use cases are CRYSTALS–KYBER (key-establishment) and CRYSTALS–Dilithium (digital signatures). In addition, the signature schemes FALCON and SPHINCS<sup>+</sup> will also be standardized. The candidates BIKE, Classic McEliece, HQC, and SIKE will all continue for further study in a fourth round of evaluation. The reasons for these choices were provided earlier in this report.
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。p.61 を描画して照合。段落ごとに分ける。

contents.html_ja: NIST は、これらのアルゴリズムの新しい標準のドラフトを、標準が仕様と一致することを確実にするために提出チームと調整しながら作成します。ドラフト作成プロセスの一環として、NIST は、特に安全性カテゴリ 1 のものについて、どの具体的なパラメータセットを含めるかに関する意見を求めます。完成したら、標準はパブリックコメントのために公開されます。コメント期間の終了後、NIST は、受け取ったフィードバックに基づいて、ドラフト標準を適宜改訂します。その後、最終的なレビュー、承認、公布のプロセスが続きます。NIST は、完成した標準を 2024 年までに公開することを望んでいます。
contents.html: NIST will create new draft standards for these algorithms, with coordination of the submission teams to ensure that the standards are in agreement with the specifications. As part of the drafting process, NIST will seek input on which specific parameter sets to include, particularly for any at security category 1. When finished, the standards will be posted for public comment. After the close of the comment period, NIST will revise the draft standards as appropriate based on the feedback received. A final review, approval, and promulgation process will then follow. NIST hopes to publish the completed standard by 2024.
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。p.61 を描画して照合。段落ごとに分ける。

contents.html_ja: 第 4 ラウンドの評価と分析は、以前のラウンドと同様に進められます。以前と同様に、4 つの候補アルゴリズムは、提出物に比較的軽微な変更を加えることが認められ、それを NIST に提出しなければならず、[9] で定義されたものと同じ要件を満たさなければなりません。さらなる詳細と指示は pqc-forum で提供されます。第 4 ラウンドの終了後、NIST は、第 4 ラウンドの候補のいくつかを標準化に選定することを決定する場合があります。
contents.html: The fourth round of evaluation and analysis will proceed similar to the earlier rounds. As before, the four candidate algorithms will be allowed to make relatively minor modifications to their submissions, which must be submitted to NIST, and must meet the same requirements as defined in [9]. Further details and instructions will be provided on the pqc-forum. After the fourth round concludes, NIST may decide to select some of the fourth round candidates for standardization.

contents.html_ja: [7] で最初に示され、第 3 ラウンドの間に強調されたとおり、
contents.html: As first indicated in [7] and emphasized during the third round:

contents.html: “NIST is pleased with the progress of the PQC standardization effort but recognizes that current and future research may lead to promising schemes which were not part of the NIST PQC Standardization Project. NIST may adopt a mechanism to accept such proposals at a later date. In particular, NIST would be interested in a general-purpose digital signature scheme which is not based on structured lattices.”
contents.html_ja: 「NIST は PQC 標準化活動の進展に満足していますが、現在および将来の研究によって、NIST PQC 標準化プロジェクトの一部ではなかった有望な方式が生まれる可能性があることを認識しています。NIST は、そのような提案を後日受け付ける仕組みを採用する場合があります。特に NIST は、構造化格子に基づかない汎用のデジタル署名方式に関心があります。」
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。p.61 を描画して照合。字下げした引用（p.62 冒頭まで）。行末の rec-ognizes を結合。

contents.html: NIST plans to issue a new Call for Proposals for public-key (quantum-resistant) digital signature algorithms in the summer of 2022. NIST primarily seeks to diversify its signature portfolio with non-structured lattice signature schemes. NIST may also be interested in signature schemes that have short signatures and fast verification. Submissions in response to this call will be due in 2023. Submitters are encouraged to communicate with NIST ahead of time. NIST will decide which (if any) of the submitted signature algorithms to accept and initiate a new process for evaluation. NIST expects this process to be much smaller in scope than the current PQC process. The signature schemes accepted to this process will need to be thoroughly analyzed, which will similarly take several years.
contents.html_ja: NIST は、2022 年夏に、公開鍵（量子耐性）デジタル署名アルゴリズムの新たな提案募集を発行する予定です。NIST は主に、構造化されていない格子の署名方式によって、署名のポートフォリオを多様化することを目指しています。NIST は、署名が短く検証が高速な署名方式にも関心を持つ場合があります。この募集に応じる提出は、2023 年が期限となります。提出者は、事前に NIST と連絡をとることが奨励されます。NIST は、提出された署名アルゴリズムのうちどれを（もしあれば）受理するかを決定し、新たな評価プロセスを開始します。NIST は、このプロセスの範囲が現在の PQC プロセスよりはるかに小さくなると見込んでいます。このプロセスに受理された署名方式は、徹底的に分析する必要があり、これにも同様に数年を要します。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。p.62 を描画して照合。段落ごとに分ける。

contents.html_ja: 第 3 ラウンドは終了し、NIST は最初の PQC 標準のドラフト作成を開始しますが、この分野の標準化の取り組みはしばらく続きます。これを、利用者が耐量子アルゴリズムの採用を待つべきという意味に解釈すべきではありません。NIST は、これら最初の標準化されたアルゴリズムが迅速に採用されることを望み、移行に関する今後のガイダンスを発行します。移行には間違いなく多くの複雑さが伴い、IoT デバイスや Certificate Transparency [285] など、一部のユースケースには課題があるでしょう。国立サイバーセキュリティ卓越センター（National Cybersecurity Center of Excellence）は、予想される移行上の課題の一部を緩和するための実践方法を開発するプロジェクトを開始しました [286, 287]。
contents.html: Even though the third round is ending and NIST will begin to draft the first PQC standards, standardization efforts in this area will continue for some time. This should not be interpreted to mean that users should wait to adopt post-quantum algorithms. NIST hopes for rapid adoption of these first standardized algorithms and will issue future guidance on the transition. The transition will undoubtedly have many complexities, and there will be challenges for some use cases, such as IoT devices or Certificate Transparency [285]. The National Cybersecurity Center of Excellence has initiated a project to develop practices to ease some of the anticipated migration challenges [286, 287].
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。p.62 を描画して照合。段落ごとに分ける。

contents.html_ja: NIST は、2022 年冬に、第 4 回 NIST PQC 標準化会議を開催する予定です。詳細は後日提供されます。
contents.html: NIST plans to host a 4th NIST PQC Standardization Conference in the winter of 2022. More details will be provided at a later date.
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。p.62 を描画して照合。段落ごとに分ける。

contents.html_ja: あらためて、NIST は、最初の 3 回のラウンドの間にコミュニティが提供したすべての研究、支援、分析に感謝します。これらの取り組みは、PQC 標準化プロセスにおける NIST にとって、不可欠なものでした。
contents.html: Once again, NIST is grateful to the community for all of the research, support, and analysis provided during the first three rounds. These efforts have been indispensable in helping NIST during the PQC standardization process.

contents.html: The RAM model. The most common cost model is the Random Access Machine (RAM) model. In this model, the cost of an attack is determined by counting operations that act on a fixed number of bits, including reading or writing to memory. The cost of memory access is assumed not to depend on the size of the memory, even when the memory is read or written in a random access fashion (i.e., a fashion where the memory address is not predictable). In the context of the NIST PQC Standardization Process, the version of the RAM model, where the operations being counted are “bit operations” that act on no more than 2 bits at a time and where each one-bit memory read or write is counted as one bit-operation, is sometimes referred to as the gate count model. This approach simplifies the cost analysis of a particular attack, as the metric does not require analyzing how memory is arranged in a physical computing system and how the distance between memory access points affects real-world costs like energy consumption and latency.
contents.html_ja: RAM モデル。最も一般的なコストモデルは、ランダムアクセスマシン（RAM）モデルです。このモデルでは、攻撃のコストは、メモリの読み書きを含む、固定ビット数に作用する演算を数えることで決まります。メモリへのアクセスのコストは、メモリがランダムアクセス方式（すなわち、メモリアドレスが予測できない方式）で読み書きされる場合であっても、メモリのサイズに依存しないものと仮定されます。NIST PQC 標準化プロセスの文脈では、数える演算が一度に 2 ビット以下に作用する「ビット演算」であり、1 ビットのメモリの読み書きがそれぞれ 1 ビット演算として数えられる RAM モデルのバージョンは、ゲート数モデルと呼ばれることがあります。この指標では、メモリが物理的な計算システムでどのように配置され、メモリアクセス点間の距離がエネルギー消費や遅延といった現実のコストにどう影響するかを分析する必要がないため、このアプローチは特定の攻撃のコスト分析を単純化します。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。p.90 を描画して照合。字下げで 2 段落に分ける。行頭の太字の小見出しは段落内の平文のまま。

contents.html_ja: RAM モデルは、大きなメモリへのアクセスのコストを小さなメモリへのアクセスよりも高くないものとして扱うため、RAM モデルでのコスト推定は、一般に、大きなメモリへのランダムアクセスを必要とする攻撃のコストを過小評価します。したがって、RAM モデルで分析したときに目標とする安全性レベルを満たすように見えるパラメータは、新たな暗号解読がない限り、安全とみなすべきです。しかし、物理的に実現可能などのメモリアーキテクチャでも、メモリへのランダムアクセスのコストはそのサイズとともに増加する可能性が高いため、RAM モデルの分析が、そのパラメータセットに対する最良の攻撃が、安全強度カテゴリの最小攻撃コストを定義するのに用いられる攻撃（総当たりの鍵探索または衝突探索）よりも安価であることを示唆している場合でも、より積極的な（そしておそらくより性能の良い）パラメータセットが目標とする安全性レベルを満たしうると主張できるかもしれません。
contents.html: Since it treats the cost of memory access to a large memory as no more expensive than memory access to a small memory, a cost estimate in the RAM model will generally underestimate the cost of attacks that require random access to a large memory. Parameters that appear to meet their targeted security level when analyzed in the RAM model should therefore be considered safe barring new cryptanalysis. However, since it is likely that the cost of randomly accessing a memory will increase with its size in any physically realizable memory architecture, it may be possible to argue that more aggressive (and presumably better performing) parameter sets can meet their targeted security levels, even when RAM model analysis suggests that the best attack on the parameter set is cheaper than the attack (brute force key search or collision search) used to define the minimum attack cost for the security strength category.

contents.html: Local models. In a local model, the distance between memory access points is considered in the cost analysis. Moving information from an initial point to a destination point requires some amount of energy and time. This cost could in fact be quite large for attacks where a significant fraction of the computations involve randomly accessing a large memory.
contents.html_ja: 局所モデル。局所モデルでは、メモリアクセス点間の距離がコスト分析で考慮されます。情報を初期点から目的点まで移動させるには、ある程度のエネルギーと時間が必要です。このコストは、計算のかなりの割合が大きなメモリへのランダムアクセスを伴う攻撃では、実際にはかなり大きくなりうるものです。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。p.90 を描画し式を拡大して照合。2 段落に分け、b0005 冒頭の文の続きを取り込み、O(√n) を LaTeX に。行末ハイフン（pub-lished、An-other）を除く。

contents.html_ja: 2 次元最近傍モデルは、メモリが 2 次元的に配置されていると仮定する局所モデルです。面積（チップやメモリボードなどの）と時間のトレードオフを見つけることでコストを削減する、ゲートの効率的なレイアウトに関する最初の研究の 1 つは、1981 年に公表されました [288]。このモデルは一般に、時間 × 面積モデルと呼ばれます。[289] が「高価なメモリモデル（Expensive Memory Model）」と呼ぶ、もう 1 つの種類の 2 次元最近傍モデルは、個々のランダムなメモリアクセスのコストが、ビットが読み書きされる場所まで、またはその場所から移動しなければならない距離に比例するという仮定の下で、メモリへのアクセスのエネルギーコストを推定しようとします。この種のモデルでは、サイズ \(n\) のメモリでビットを読み書きするコストは、\(\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{n})\) ビット演算に相当します。
contents.html: 2D nearest neighbor models are local models that assume that memory is arranged in a two-dimensional fashion. One of the first studies on efficient layouts of gates to reduce costs by finding tradeoffs between area (of a chip, memory board, etc.) and time was published in 1981 [288]. This model is commonly referred to as the time × area model. Another type of 2D-nearest neighbor model, referred to by [289] as the “Expensive Memory Model,” attempts to estimate the energy cost of accessing memory under the assumption that the cost of each random memory access is proportional to the distance that a bit must travel to or from the location where it is read or written. In this type of model, the cost of reading or writing a bit in a memory of size \(n\) would be equivalent to \(\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{n})\) bit operations.

contents.html: An estimate for the value of the hidden constant can be found in [60, Section 6.6]. It should be noted that this estimate is based on the density of Dynamic Random Access Memory (DRAM) and the per-distance energy cost of moving data via electric signals through on-die wires and so may not be accurate where other technologies can be used. For large memories, perhaps several petabytes, it would likely make sense to transmit data via fiber optics, which incur some additional costs at their endpoints but consume significantly less energy per bandwidth per unit distance. For even larger memories, it would likely make sense to use a memory technology that is denser and cheaper to manufacture but slower and more expensive to read/write than DRAM. Examples of such memory technologies are hard disk and flash memory.
contents.html_ja: 隠れた定数の値の推定は [60, Section 6.6] にあります。この推定は、ダイナミックランダムアクセスメモリ（DRAM）の密度と、ダイ上の配線を通じて電気信号でデータを移動させる際の距離あたりのエネルギーコストに基づいているため、他の技術が使える場合には正確でない可能性がある点に注意すべきです。数ペタバイトにもなりうる大規模なメモリでは、光ファイバーを介してデータを伝送することが理にかなう可能性が高く、光ファイバーは終端で追加のコストを伴うものの、帯域幅・単位距離あたりのエネルギー消費が大幅に少なくなります。さらに大規模なメモリでは、DRAM よりも高密度で製造が安価である一方、読み書きが遅く高価なメモリ技術を使うことが理にかなう可能性が高いでしょう。そのようなメモリ技術の例は、ハードディスクとフラッシュメモリです。

contents.html_ja: 3 次元最近傍モデルは、メモリボードが 3 次元的に配置されて接続されていると考える局所モデルです [290]。このような配置は、2 次元モデルと比べて、メモリの任意のビットに対する「近傍」の数を増やし、コストを \(\mathcal{O}(\sqrt[3]{n})\) に減らします。積層されたメモリボードの構造では熱が容易かつ迅速には放散できないため、メモリへのアクセス頻度や、メモリ技術がアイドル時に熱を発生するかどうかによっては、冷却を待つための遅延時間が、2 次元から 3 次元モデルへのコスト削減を相殺しうることが指摘されています。
contents.html: 3D nearest neighbor models are local models that consider memory boards connected in a three-dimensional arrangement [290]. Such an arrangement increases the number of “near neighbors” to any particular bit of memory relative to the 2D model, reducing the cost to \(\mathcal{O}(\sqrt[3]{n})\). It has been noted that heat cannot easily or quickly dissipate in a stacked memory board structure, so possible time delays to allow for cooling could potentially cancel out the cost reduction from the 2D to 3D model, depending on how often the memory needs to be accessed and whether the memory technology generates heat when it is idle.

contents.html: Other cost models Fixed Budget models measure an attack by limiting the attacker to a fixed budget, and estimating the time required to execute the attack given the budget. Van Orschoot and Weiner included budget-based examples in their analyses of parallel collision search [291, 292] and in 2020, Longa et al. used a budget-based cost model to consider attacks on SIKE [227].
contents.html_ja: その他のコストモデル。固定予算モデルは、攻撃者の予算を一定に制限し、その予算で攻撃を実行するのに必要な時間を推定することで、攻撃を評価します。Van Orschoot と Weiner は、並列衝突探索の分析 [291, 292] に予算ベースの例を含め、2020 年には Longa らが、SIKE に対する攻撃を検討するために予算ベースのコストモデルを使用しました [227]。

contents.html_ja: このアプローチは、検討する予算の範囲内で、せいぜい数年程度の時間スケールで攻撃を実行できる場合には、リスクを判断する現実的な方法を与えるといえます。しかし、非常に長い時間の推定は、おそらく意味を持ちません。攻撃者は、攻撃の実装を始める前に技術が向上するのを待つほうがよい結果になりうるためです。非常に長い時間の推定は、攻撃を評価する際に、より大きな予算を検討すべきことを示すサインかもしれません。さらに、長い時間スケールの攻撃で検討される小さな予算は、しばしば幻想です。特に、評価されたコストに電力消費とハードウェア交換のコストが含まれていない場合、数年を超える攻撃では、それらが確実にハードウェアへの初期投資を上回るでしょう。検討する予算を非常に長い時間スケールが必要になるほどに制限すると、その正味の効果として、メモリがランダムアクセスで使われるか局所的に使われるかにかかわらず、大量のメモリを必要とする攻撃のコストを過大評価することになります。
contents.html: This approach arguably gives a realistic way of determining risk, when an attack can be executed within the considered budget on a timescale of no more than a few years. However, very long time estimates are likely not meaningful, because an attacker may do better by waiting for technology to improve before beginning to implement the attack. Very long time estimates may also be a sign that a larger budget should be considered when evaluating the attack. Moreover, the small budget considered in long-time-scale attacks is often illusory, in particular when evaluated costs do not include power consumption and hardware replacement costs, which surely would dominate over any initial investment in hardware for any attack lasting more than a few years. If the considered budget is restricted to the point where a very long time scale is required, the net effect will be to overestimate the cost of attacks that require a lot of memory, whether that memory is accessed in a random access or a local fashion.

contents.html: The quantum circuit model. The most common model used for giving concrete quantum resource estimates is the quantum circuit model. In this model, a computation is described by a series of transformations (typically unitary gates) acting on some number of qubits. Each gate acts on at most two qubits at a time with no locality restriction. This is similar to the classical circuit model, where Boolean logic gates act on classical bits. While circuit models are non-local models in their most basic form, they differ significantly from RAM models in that an operation equivalent to a serial random access to a memory of size \(M\) would generally require \(M\) gates. As demonstrated by [293] this cost can be amortized if multiple processes are accessing the memory in parallel. As with the RAM model, a local version of the circuit model may be considered, where qubits are assumed to be arranged in a two-dimensional or three-dimensional grid, and gates can only be performed between nearby qubits.
contents.html_ja: 量子回路モデル。具体的な量子資源の推定を与えるために使われる最も一般的なモデルは、量子回路モデルです。このモデルでは、計算は、ある数の量子ビットに作用する一連の変換（通常はユニタリゲート）で記述されます。各ゲートは、局所性の制約なしに、一度に多くても 2 つの量子ビットに作用します。これは、ブールの論理ゲートが古典ビットに作用する、古典的な回路モデルに似ています。回路モデルは最も基本的な形では非局所モデルですが、サイズ \(M\) のメモリへの逐次的なランダムアクセスに相当する操作が、一般に \(M\) 個のゲートを必要とする点で、RAM モデルとは大きく異なります。[293] が示したように、複数のプロセスがメモリに並列にアクセスする場合には、このコストを償却できます。RAM モデルと同様に、量子ビットが 2 次元または 3 次元の格子状に配置され、ゲートが近くの量子ビット間でしか実行できないと仮定する、回路モデルの局所版も考えられます。

contents.html_ja: 量子アルゴリズムの資源コストは、しばしば論理レベルで（すなわち、量子ビットとゲートが本質的に完全であるという仮定の下で）評価されます。あるいは、物理レベルで資源コストを評価すること、すなわち、現実の不完全な量子ビットやゲートから、ほぼ完全な量子ビットやゲートを構築するコストを考慮することもできます。中間的な選択肢は、論理レベルでコストを評価しつつ、Clifford ゲート（通常、量子耐故障方式では安価です）を、T ゲート（通常、はるかに高価です）とは別に数えることです。
contents.html: The resource costs of quantum algorithms are often assessed at the logical level (i.e., under the assumption that qubits and gates are essentially perfect). Alternatively, one can choose to assess resource costs at the physical level, i.e., considering the costs of constructing near-perfect qubits and gates from their real, imperfect analogues. An intermediate option is to assess costs at the logical level, but to count Clifford gates (which are typically cheap in quantum fault-tolerance schemes) differently from T gates (which are typically much more expensive.)

contents.html_ja: NIST PQC の提案募集 [9] は、敵対者が直列に実行できるゲートが MAXDEPTH 個以下に制限される、量子回路モデルの変種を強調していました。これは、並列化がうまくいかないことが知られている AES や SHA に対する量子攻撃と比較する際に、特に関連します。
contents.html: The NIST PQC call for proposals [9] highlighted a variant of the quantum circuit model where the adversary is limited to performing no more than MAXDEPTH gates in series. This is particularly relevant when making comparisons to quantum attacks on AES and SHA, which are known to not parallelize well.

contents.html: The Quantum RAM model. The quantum RAM model [294] generalizes the classical RAM model to quantum computation and is used fairly often in giving asymptotic costs for quantum attacks. A logarithmic cost for RAM queries was proposed by [294] based on an idealized “Bucket-Brigade” architecture. However, it was argued by [295] that for large quantum computations, such as those needed in cryptanalysis, a Bucket-Brigade memory would require active error correction, yielding a similar cost for RAM access as predicted by the quantum circuit model. More recent analysis [296] has suggested that the Bucket Brigade architecture has an advantage over other architectures for emulating quantum RAM even where error correction is required, although it does not contradict the claim of [295] that a quantum memory that needs to be accessed a large number of times will require a number of active gates comparable to the size of the memory.
contents.html_ja: 量子 RAM モデル。量子 RAM モデル [294] は、古典的な RAM モデルを量子計算に一般化したもので、量子攻撃の漸近的なコストを示す際にかなり頻繁に用いられます。RAM 問い合わせの対数的なコストは、理想化された「バケツリレー（Bucket-Brigade）」アーキテクチャに基づいて [294] により提案されました。しかし、[295] は、暗号解読に必要なような大規模な量子計算では、バケツリレー型メモリは能動的な誤り訂正を必要とし、量子回路モデルが予測するものと同様の RAM アクセスのコストをもたらすと論じました。より最近の分析 [296] は、誤り訂正が必要な場合でも、バケツリレーアーキテクチャが量子 RAM のエミュレーションにおいて他のアーキテクチャより優位性を持つことを示唆していますが、何度もアクセスする必要のある量子メモリには、メモリのサイズに匹敵する数の能動的なゲートが必要になるという [295] の主張と矛盾するものではありません。

contents.html: C. On the Concrete Intractability of Finding Short Lattice Vectors
contents.html_ja: C. 短い格子ベクトル探索の具体的な困難性
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。p.92 を描画して照合。付録 C の見出し。

contents.html: The standard method for finding short lattice vectors, the BKZ (Block Korkine-Zolotarev) algorithm [297], was developed by Schnorr and Euchner in 1991. The BKZ algorithm solves the \(\gamma\)-approximate SVP problem<sup>16</sup> for lattices with large dimension, \(d\), by iteratively calling an “oracle” for solving the SVP problem in sub-lattices of smaller dimension, \(\beta\) – gradually improving the “quality” of the lattice basis by finding vectors that are shorter and more nearly orthogonal to each other.
contents.html_ja: 短い格子ベクトルを見つける標準的な方法である BKZ（Block Korkine-Zolotarev）アルゴリズム [297] は、1991 年に Schnorr と Euchner によって開発されました。BKZ アルゴリズムは、次元 \(d\) の大きな格子に対する \(\gamma\)-近似 SVP 問題<sup>16</sup>を、より小さな次元 \(\beta\) の部分格子における SVP 問題を解く「オラクル」を反復的に呼び出すことで解きます。その際、より短く、互いにより直交に近いベクトルを見つけることで、格子基底の「品質」を徐々に改善します。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。p.92–93 を描画して照合。2 段落に分け、脚注番号 16 を上付きに、γ・d・β を数式に。p.93 冒頭の続きを取り込み、[298–302] の行折り返しの空白を除く。

contents.html_ja: SVP の「オラクル」を実装するために使える格子簡約アルゴリズムには、列挙とふるい分け（sieving）の 2 種類があります。列挙アルゴリズム（たとえば [298–302] を参照）は必要なメモリ量が小さいものの、実行時間は \(\beta\) に関して超指数的です。ふるい分けアルゴリズム（たとえば [303–305] を参照）は、実行時間が \(\beta\) に関して指数的ですが、指数的な量のメモリも必要とします。次元が小さい場合は列挙アルゴリズムがふるい分けアルゴリズムより優れていますが、次元が大きくなるにつれてふるい分けのほうが優れた性能を示します。少なくともこれらのアルゴリズムの古典的実装では、暗号に用いられる次元において、ふるい分けのほうが優れた性能を示します [300]。列挙アルゴリズムの量子実装が、特定の格子パラメータセットがカテゴリ 2 または 4 を満たせるかどうかに影響する可能性はありますが、既知の量子高速化は十分小さいため、カテゴリ 1、3、5 を満たすのに十分な古典的安全性を持つパラメータセットは、量子攻撃を考慮してもこれらの目標を満たすはずです。ふるい分けアルゴリズムの性能は向上してきました [306–314] が、最近の成果 [315] は、これまでふるい分けの漸近的計算量を最も大きく低下させてきた局所性鋭敏型ハッシュ手法は、これ以上改良できないことを示しています。
contents.html: There are two types of lattice reduction algorithms that may be used to implement the SVP “oracle,” enumeration and sieving. Enumeration algorithms (see, for example, [298–302]) require small amounts of memory but have run times that are super-exponential in \(\beta\). Sieving algorithms (see, for example [303–305]) have run times that are exponential in \(\beta\), but also require an exponential amount of memory. While enumeration algorithms outperform sieving algorithms for smaller dimensions, sieving performs better as the dimension increases. At least in the case of classical implementations of these algorithms, sieving performs better at dimensions that are used for cryptography [300]. While it is possible that quantum implementations of enumeration algorithms may affect whether it is possible for certain lattice parameter sets to meet category 2 or 4, the known quantum speedups are small enough that parameter sets with enough classical security to meet categories 1, 3, and 5 should also meet these targets when quantum attacks are considered. The performance of sieving algorithms has been improving [306–314], however recent results [315] indicate that improvements in locally sensitive hash techniques, which have resulted in the largest decreases in asymptotic complexity for sieving thus far, cannot be improved further.

contents.html: 16 The \(\gamma\)-approximate SVP problem involves finding a vector that is at most \(\gamma\) times longer than the shortest vector. This is a search problem and is closely related to the decision problem GapSVP.
contents.html_ja: 16 \(\gamma\)-近似 SVP 問題は、最短ベクトルの高々 \(\gamma\) 倍の長さのベクトルを見つけることを含みます。これは探索問題であり、判定問題 GapSVP と密接に関連しています。

contents.html_ja: BKZ と、SVP の「オラクル」の実装に用いられるふるい分けアルゴリズムはヒューリスティックなアルゴリズムであるため、BKZ の実行コストの推定は、さまざまな理由で難しい場合があります。特に、暗号に関連するサイズの次元でのこれらのアルゴリズムの振る舞いが、理論的な上界・下界とは異なり、計算可能な小さな問題インスタンスでの振る舞いとも異なるため、そうです。ふるい分けアルゴリズムの具体的な困難性の推定には、必要となる大量のメモリを考慮することも必要です（付録 B を参照）。
contents.html: BKZ and the sieving algorithms used to implement the SVP “oracle” are heuristic algorithms, and so estimating the cost of running BKZ can be tricky for various reasons. This is particularly the case since the behavior of these algorithms for dimensions of sizes relevant to cryptography is different from theoretical upper and lower bounds, and is also different from their behavior for small problem instances that are computationally tractable. Estimating the concrete hardness of sieving algorithms also requires accounting for the large amount of memory required (see Appendix B).
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。p.92–94 を描画して照合。脚注 16 と本文 5 段落に分ける（冒頭の「but also require…」は b0004 へ移した）。最後の段落は p.94 冒頭の続き（p93-b0002 内）を取り込む。行末ハイフン（algo-rithms、Esti-mating、short-est、practi-cal、quan-tum）を除く。

contents.html_ja: BKZ のコストを推定するために一般に使われるアプローチの 1 つは、問題のコア SVP の困難性 [156, Section 6.1] を決定することです。BKZ の実行には多項式回数の「オラクル」呼び出しが必要です [316] が、必要な呼び出し回数を正確に決定することは困難な場合があります。コア SVP 手法は、暗号解読に有用な解を見つけるのに必要な \(\beta\) の値を推定した後、次元 \(\beta\) の SVP「オラクル」を 1 回呼び出すコストのみを推定することで、この煩雑さを避けます。さまざまな暗号システムのコア SVP 困難性を比較することは、それらの相対的な安全性レベルの比較に有用ですが（表 10 と表 11 を参照）、このアプローチは必然的に、BKZ アルゴリズムの実行コストを過小評価します。
contents.html: One commonly-used approach for estimating the cost of BKZ involves determining the core SVP hardness [156, Section 6.1] of the problem. While solving BKZ requires a polynomial number of calls to the “oracle” [316], determining the exact number of calls required can be difficult. The core SVP method avoids this complication by only estimating the cost of a single call to the SVP “oracle” in dimension \(\beta\), after estimating the value of \(\beta\) that is required to find a solution that is useful for cryptanalysis. While comparing the core SVP hardness of various cryptosystems can be useful in comparing their relative security levels (see Tables 10 and 11), this approach necessarily underestimates the cost of running the BKZ algorithm.

contents.html_ja: 過去 10 年間に、暗号システムで使われる次元の格子上での BKZ アルゴリズムの振る舞いの理解が進み [317–320]、格子ベース暗号システムの具体的な安全性の判定を助けるツールも利用可能になっています [321]。<sup>17</sup> その結果、格子ベース暗号システムの具体的な安全性の理解は、過去数年間で大きく改善されました。
contents.html: Over the past decade, work has progressed in understanding the behavior of the BKZ algorithm on lattices of dimensions that are used in cryptosystems [317–320], and tools are available to aid in determining the concrete security of lattice-based cryptosystems [321].<sup>17</sup> As a result, understanding of the concrete security of lattice-based cryptosystems has greatly improved over the past several years.
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。p.92–94 を描画して照合。脚注 16 と本文 5 段落に分ける（冒頭の「but also require…」は b0004 へ移した）。最後の段落は p.94 冒頭の続き（p93-b0002 内）を取り込む。行末ハイフン（algo-rithms、Esti-mating、short-est、practi-cal、quan-tum）を除く。

contents.html_ja: 多くの格子ベース暗号システムは、Ring-LWE や Module-LWE のような代数的構造を持つ問題に基づいています。これらの問題は、イデアル格子やモジュール格子のような代数的構造を持つ格子に関わる最短ベクトル問題の変種、つまりイデアル SVP 問題やモジュール SVP 問題に関連しています。BKZ アルゴリズムは、イデアル格子やモジュール格子に存在する構造を利用しません。しかし、実用的な暗号解読の目的では、そのような格子上で BKZ を上回るアルゴリズムが存在することを示唆する証拠は得られていません。
contents.html: Many lattice-based cryptosystems are based on problems that have algebraic structure, such as Ring-LWE or Module-LWE. These problems are connected to variants of the shortest vector problem that involve lattices with algebraic structure, such as ideal and module lattices, and the ideal and module SVP problems. The BKZ algorithm does not exploit the structure that is present in ideal or module lattices. However, for the purposes of practical cryptanalysis, there is no available evidence to suggest that algorithms that outperform BKZ on such lattices exist.
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。p.92–94 を描画して照合。脚注 16 と本文 5 段落に分ける（冒頭の「but also require…」は b0004 へ移した）。最後の段落は p.94 冒頭の続き（p93-b0002 内）を取り込む。行末ハイフン（algo-rithms、Esti-mating、short-est、practi-cal、quan-tum）を除く。

contents.html_ja: それでも、理論的な観点からは、近似比 \(\gamma\) が緩やかに準指数的である \(\gamma\)-近似イデアル SVP を解く、多項式時間の量子アルゴリズムが存在することに注意することが重要です [322]。この近似比は、任意の固定ブロックサイズの BKZ が達成する近似比よりも漸近的には優れていますが、格子の次元とブロックサイズが、実用的な格子ベース暗号システムに対する攻撃の典型的な範囲にあるときは、BKZ より劣るように見えます [323]。したがって、この量子アルゴリズムの存在は、格子ベース暗号システムの実用上の安全性に影響しないようです。加えて、このアルゴリズムで用いられる手法は、イデアル格子の乗法的構造に大きく依存しており、ランク 2 以上のモジュール格子には直接適用できないようです。したがって、これらの手法が、第 3 ラウンドの候補（たとえば Ring LWE、NTRU、Module LWE）のいずれの困難性の仮定にも、漸近的にさえ、直接影響することは知られていません。<sup>18</sup>
contents.html: Nonetheless, from a theoretical perspective, it is important to note that there is a quantum algorithm that runs in polynomial time and solves \(\gamma\)-approximate ideal SVP with an approximation ratio \(\gamma\) that is mildly subexponential [322]. This approximation ratio is asymptotically better than the approximation ratio achieved by BKZ with any fixed block size; but it appears to be worse than BKZ when the lattice dimension and block size are in the typical range for attacks on practical lattice-based cryptosystems [323]. Hence, the existence of this quantum algorithm does not appear to impact the practical security of lattice-based cryptosystems. In addition, the techniques used in this algorithm rely heavily on the multiplicative structure of ideal lattices, and do not seem to be directly applicable to module lattices of rank 2 or more. Hence these techniques are not known to directly impact the hardness assumptions of any of the round 3 candidates (e.g., Ring LWE, NTRU, Module LWE), even asymptotically.<sup>18</sup>

contents.html_ja: 最近関心が持たれている分野の 1 つは、S-unit 攻撃 [324, 325] と「Twisted-PHS」アルゴリズム [326–328] で、これらは \(\gamma\)-近似イデアル SVP の量子アルゴリズムの一般化とみなせます。これらのアルゴリズムは、見つかる解の品質を改善するために、計算集約的な前処理ステップを使用します。これらのアルゴリズムが近似比 \(\gamma\) をわずかに改善する可能性を示唆する証拠はありますが、これが \(\gamma\) の（次元 \(n\) の関数としての）漸近的なスケーリングを準指数から多項式に変えることを示す証拠はほとんどありません。したがって、これらの改善は理論的には興味深いものの、格子ベース暗号システムに対する実用的な攻撃につながる可能性は低いと思われます。
contents.html: One area of recent interest is S-unit attacks [324, 325] and the “Twisted-PHS” algorithm [326–328], which can be viewed as generalizations of the quantum algorithm for \(\gamma\)-approximate ideal SVP. These algorithms use a computationally-intensive pre-processing step to improve the quality of the solution that is found. Some evidence suggests that these algorithms may achieve mild improvements in the approximation ratio \(\gamma\), but there is little evidence that this will change the asymptotic scaling of \(\gamma\) from subexponential to polynomial (as a function of the dimension \(n\)). Hence these improvements are of theoretical interest, but seem unlikely to lead to practical attacks on lattice-based cryptosystems.

contents.html: Miccancio [149] introduced a ring-based analogue of Ajtai’s SIS problem in 2002. A ring-based analogue of LWE (and an associated public-key encryption scheme) was introduced by Lyubashevsky, Peikert, and Regev [152] in 2010. Further, an algebraically-structured (and in particular, module-based) formulation of SIS/LWE-type problems – which can be syntactically viewed as interpolating between the original integer-based presentation and the later polynomial-ring-based presentations – was first introduced by Brakerski, Gentry, and Vaikuntanathan [153] in 2011 under the name General Learning With Errors.

contents.html: Miccancio [149] introduced a ring-based analogue of Ajtai’s SIS problem in 2002. A search variant of ring-based LWE (and an associated public-key encryption scheme, relying on the Goldreich-Levin hardcore function [150]) was introduced by Stehle, Steinfeld, Tanaka, and Xagawa [151] in 2009. A decisional variant of Ring-LWE with associated public-key encryption scheme (and an associated search-to-decision reduction) was introduced by Lyubashevsky, Peikert, and Regev [152] in 2010. Further, an algebraically-structured (and in particular, module-based) formulation of SIS/LWE-type problems – which can be syntactically viewed as interpolating between the original integer-based presentation and the later polynomial-ring-based presentations – was first introduced by Brakerski, Gentry, and Vaikuntanathan [153] in 2011 under the name General Learning With Errors.
contents.html_ja: Miccancio [149] は 2002 年に、Ajtai の SIS 問題の環ベースの類似物を導入しました。環ベースの LWE の探索版（および、Goldreich-Levin のハードコア関数 [150] に依拠する関連の公開鍵暗号方式）は、2009 年に Stehle、Steinfeld、Tanaka、Xagawa [151] により導入されました。関連する公開鍵暗号方式（および関連する探索から判定への帰着）を伴う Ring-LWE の判定版は、2010 年に Lyubashevsky、Peikert、Regev [152] により導入されました。さらに、SIS/LWE 型の問題を代数的に構造化した（特にモジュールベースの）定式化は、構文上は元の整数ベースの表現と後の多項式環ベースの表現との間を補間するものとみなせますが、2011 年に Brakerski、Gentry、Vaikuntanathan [153] により General Learning With Errors という名称で初めて導入されました。

Reports on Computer Systems Technology

The Information Technology Laboratory (ITL) at the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) promotes the U.S. economy and public welfare by providing technical leadership for the Nation’s measurement and standards infrastructure. ITL develops tests, test methods, reference data, proof of concept implementations, and technical analyses to advance the development and productive use of information technology. ITL’s responsi-bilities include the development of management, administrative, technical, and physical standards and guidelines for the cost-effective security and privacy of other than national security-related information in federal information systems.
Abstract

The National Institute of Standards and Technology is in the process of selecting public-key cryptographic algorithms through a public, competition-like process. The new public-key cryptography standards will specify additional digital signature, public-key encryp-tion, and key-establishment algorithms to augment Federal Information Processing Stan-dard (FIPS) 186-4, Digital Signature Standard (DSS), as well as NIST Special Publication (SP) 800-56A Revision 3, Recommendation for Pair-Wise Key-Establishment Schemes Us-ing Discrete Logarithm Cryptography, and SP 800-56B Revision 2, Recommendation for Pair-Wise Key Establishment Using Integer Factorization Cryptography. It is intended that these algorithms will be capable of protecting sensitive information well into the foresee-able future, including after the advent of quantum computers. This report describes the evaluation and selection process of the NIST Post-Quantum Cryptography Standardization process third-round candidates based on public feedback and internal review. The report summarizes each of the 15 third-round candidate algorithms and identifies those selected for standardization, as well as those that will continue to be evaluated in a fourth round of analysis. The public-key encryption and key-establishment algorithm that will be standardized is CRYSTALS–KYBER. The digital signatures that will be standardized are CRYSTALS–Dilithium, FALCON, and SPHINCS+. While there are multiple signature algorithms selected, NIST recommends CRYSTALS–Dilithium as the primary algorithm to be implemented. In addition, four of the alternate key-establishment candidate algorithms will advance to a fourth round of evaluation: BIKE, Classic McEliece, HQC, and SIKE. These candidates are still being considered for future standardization. NIST will also issue a new Call for Proposals for public-key digital signature algorithms to augment and diversify its signature portfolio.
Keywords
cryptography; digital signatures; key-encapsulation mechanism (KEM); key-establishment; post-quantum cryptography; public-key encryption; quantum resistant; quantum safe

Introduction

Over the past several years, there has been steady progress toward building quantum com-puters. The security of many commonly used public-key cryptosystems would be at risk if large-scale quantum computers were ever realized. In particular, this would include key-establishment schemes and digital signatures that are based on factoring, discrete log-arithms, and elliptic curve cryptography. In contrast, symmetric cryptographic primitives, such as block ciphers and hash functions, would not be as drastically impacted. As a result, there has been intensified research into finding public-key cryptosystems that would be se-cure against adversaries with both quantum and classical computers. This field is often referred to as post-quantum cryptography (PQC), or sometimes quantum-resistant cryp-tography. The goal is to develop schemes that can be deployed in existing communication networks and protocols without significant modifications. In response, the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) initiated a public, competition-like process to select quantum-resistant public-key cryptographic al-gorithms. The new public-key cryptography standards will specify algorithms for digital signatures, public-key encryption, and key establishment. The new standards will aug-ment Federal Information Processing Standard (FIPS) 186-4, Digital Signature Standard (DSS) [1], Special Publication (SP) 800-56A Revision 3, Recommendation for Pair-Wise Key-Establishment Schemes Using Discrete Logarithm Cryptography [2], and SP 800-56B Revision 2, Recommendation for Pair-Wise Key Establishment Using Integer Factorization Cryptography [3]. It is intended that these algorithms will be capable of protecting sen-sitive U.S. Government information well into the foreseeable future, including after the advent of quantum computers. The process will be referred to as the NIST Post-Quantum Cryptography Standardization Process hereafter in this document. NIST issued a public call for submissions to the PQC Standardization Process in De-cember 2016 [4]. Prior to the November 2017 deadline a total of 82 candidate algorithms were submitted. Shortly thereafter, the 69 candidates that met both the submission re-quirements and the minimum acceptability criteria were accepted into the first round of the standardization process. Submission packages for the first-round candidates were posted online for public review and comment [5]. After a year-long review of the candidates, NIST selected 26 algorithms to move on to the second round of evaluation in January 2019 [6]. These algorithms were viewed as the most promising candidates for eventual standardization, and were selected based on both internal analysis and public feedback. During the second round, there was continued evaluation by NIST and the broader cryptographic community. After careful deliberation, NIST selected seven finalists and eight alternates to move on to the third round in July 2020 [7]. NIST’s intent was to standardize a small number of the finalists at the end of the third round, as well as a small number of the alternate candidates after a fourth round. The third round began in July 2020 and continued for approximately 18 months. During the third round, there was a more thorough analysis of the theoretical and empirical evi-dence used to justify the security of the candidates. There was also careful benchmarking of their performance using optimized implementations on a variety of software and hard-ware platforms. Similar to the first two rounds, NIST also held the (virtual) Third NIST PQC Standardization Conference in June 2021. Each of the finalists and alternates were invited to present an update on their candidate algorithm. In addition, several researchers presented work that was relevant to the PQC standardization process. After three rounds of evaluation and analysis, NIST has selected the first algorithms it will standardize as a result of the PQC Standardization Process. The public-key encapsu-lation mechanism (KEM) that will be standardized is CRYSTALS–KYBER.1 The digital signatures that will be standardized are CRYSTALS–Dilithium, FALCON, and SPHINCS+. While there are multiple signature algorithms selected, NIST recommends CRYSTALS– Dilithium as the primary algorithm to be implemented. In addition, four of the alternate KEM candidate algorithms will advance to a fourth round of evaluation: BIKE, Classic McEliece, HQC, and SIKE. These candidates will be considered for future standardization at the conclusion of the fourth round. 1.1 Purpose and Organization of this Document

The purpose of this document is to report on the third round of the NIST PQC Standard-ization Process. The report is organized as follows. Section 2 enumerates the candidates that were included in the third round. Descriptions of the evaluation criteria and selection process used to ultimately select from the third-round finalists and alternate candidates are then provided. The algorithms that will be standardized are then named, along with the candidates moving into a fourth round of evaluation and analysis. Section 3 contains some technical material relevant to the candidate algorithms. This includes a brief explanation of the underlying security problems, as well as the definitions of various computational models that NIST used in its evaluation. Section 4 summarizes each of the third-round candidates. For each candidate, there is a brief description of the algorithm and its characteristics. This report presents reasons why candidate algorithms were either selected for standardization (or the fourth round), as well as reasons why the other candidate algorithms were not selected. Section 5 describes the next steps in the NIST PQC Standardization Process. More details are provided on standardizing the algorithms selected, and on the process for eval-uating candidate algorithms selected for the fourth round. Section 5 also mentions a new Call for Proposals for public-key digital signature algorithms.
Evaluation Criteria and the Selection Process
2.1 Acceptance of the Third-Round Candidates

NIST selected 15 candidate algorithms for the third round. Seven of the 15 algorithms were chosen to be ‘finalists,’ while the other eight algorithms were labelled ‘alternates’ [7]. The set of finalists included the algorithms that NIST considered to be the most promising to fit the majority of use cases and the most likely to be ready for standardization soon after the end of the third round. The alternate candidates were regarded as potential candidates for future standardization, most likely after another round of evaluation. Some of the alter-nate candidates have worse performance characteristics than the finalists but might yet be selected for standardization based on NIST’s high confidence in their security. Others have acceptable performance but require additional analysis or other work to inspire sufficient confidence in their security for NIST to standardize. In addition, some alternate candidates were selected based either on NIST’s desire for diversity in future post-quantum security standards or on their potential for further improvement. The seven finalists included four key encapsulation mechanisms (KEMs), and three digital signature mechanisms. Of the eight alternates, five were KEMs and three were dig-ital signatures. Submission teams were allowed to make minor modifications and resubmit their packages, which had to meet the same requirements as the original submissions. The complete updated specifications were posted on NIST’s PQC website [5] on October 23, 2020, for public review.

2.2 Evaluation Criteria

NIST’s Call for Proposals identified three broad aspects of the evaluation criteria that would be used to compare candidate algorithms throughout the NIST PQC Standardization Pro-cess: 1) security, 2) cost and performance, and 3) algorithm and implementation character-istics. These criteria are described below, along with a discussion of how they impacted the third-round candidate evaluations.
2.2.1 Security

As was the case for the past Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) and Secure Hash Algo-rithm 3 (SHA-3) competitions, security is the most important criterion that NIST uses when evaluating candidate post-quantum algorithms. NIST’s public-key standards are currently utilized in a wide variety of applications, including internet protocols like TLS, SSH, IKE, IPsec, and DNSSEC, as well as for certificates, software code signing, and secure boot-loaders. The new NIST public-key standards will provide post-quantum security for each of these applications. For the purpose of quantifying the security of candidate algorithms, NIST gave three possible security definitions—two for encryption and one for signatures. NIST also des-ignated five security strength categories for classifying the computational complexity of attacks that violate the security definitions (see [9]).

NIST also mentioned other desirable security properties, such as forward secrecy, resis-tance to side-channel and multi-key attacks, and resistance to misuse, all of which continue to be of interest. In some cases, NIST has encouraged submitters to make minor tweaks to provide or enhance these additional desirable security properties (e.g., by adding a public salt to ciphertexts to avoid multi-target attacks against KEMs). For general-use encryption and key-establishment schemes, the Call for Proposals [9] asked for “semantically secure” schemes with respect to adaptive chosen ciphertext at-tack (equivalently, IND-CCA2 security). For ephemeral use cases, NIST also accepted algorithms that provided semantic security with respect to chosen plaintext attack (equiv-alently, IND-CPA security). IND-CCA2 security is not required in strictly ephemeral use cases and attempting to meet the more stringent requirements of IND-CCA2 security may incur significant performance penalties for some schemes. Digital signature schemes were required to provide existentially unforgeable signatures with respect to an adaptive cho-sen message attack (EUF-CMA security). Submitters were encouraged but not required to provide proofs of security in relevant models. The five security strength categories defined in [9] were based on the computational re-sources required to perform certain brute-force attacks against the existing NIST standards for AES and SHA in a variety of different models of the cost of computation, both classical and quantum. In some cases, questions have arisen regarding whether various parameter sets meet their claimed security strength categories. The uncertainty arises principally from two distinct considerations. First, the NIST security strength categories are defined in a way that leaves open the relative cost of various computational resources, including quantum gates, classical gates, quantum memory, classical memory, hardware, energy, and time. The idea is that in order to meet, for example, category 1, the best attack violating the security definition of a pa-rameter set should cost more than a brute-force key search attack on a single instance of AES-128, according to any plausible assumption regarding the relative cost of the various computational resources involved in a real-world attack. Different opinions can therefore arise regarding what constitutes a plausible assumption regarding the relative cost of com-putational resources. Second, even if one has agreed upon a model or a range of models for evaluating the relative cost of various computational resources, there may still be uncertainty how much of a given resource an attack actually requires. For example, many parameters of lattice reduction attacks (such as the BKZ block size, the number of required BKZ iterations, or the number of dimensions for free) are not proven optimal values but rather heuristic estimates based on simplified models, simulations, and mathematical conjectures. Addi-tionally, while some submitters have rightly observed that many widely used cost models, such as the RAM model, underestimate the difficulty of certain memory intensive attacks, the comparative lack of published cryptanalysis using more realistic models may bring into question whether sufficient effort has been made to optimize the best-known attacks to perform well in these models. Submitters were asked to provide a preliminary classification of all proposed parameter sets according to the definitions of the five security strength categories. While category 1, 2, and 3 parameters were (and continue to be) the most important targets for NIST’s evaluation, NIST nevertheless strongly encouraged the submitters to provide at least one parameter set that meets category 5. Aside from NTRU, all of the third-round submission packages contained parameters that claimed to meet category 5. In June 2021, at NIST’s request, the NTRU team announced parameters designed to meet category 5 given the state of the art in lattice cryptanalysis [10]. During the first, second, and third rounds of the NIST standardization process, a num-ber of cryptanalytic results dramatically reduced the security assumed for some submitted schemes and undermined NIST’s confidence in the maturity of others. These results were the basis for many of NIST’s decisions thus far in the process, particularly for Rainbow and GeMSS [11–13]. Cryptanalysis has also brought some of the candidates’ security cat-egory claims into question or shown them to be false. In response, NIST may move some parameter sets down to a lower category (or refrain from standardizing them) if warranted. Progress was also made in clarifying some outstanding security questions during the third round. In lattice-based cryptography, methods were developed to replace the asymp-totic security estimates represented by the core SVP methodology with concrete security estimates expressed as a gate count that can be more directly compared with security esti-mates for the non-lattice candidates (see [14, 15], as well as discussion on the pqc-forum [16]). Several of the finalists have also been implemented with countermeasures to side-channel attacks (see Section 2.2.3). Additionally, further investigations have been per-formed to determine whether the BIKE submission’s estimate of its decryption failure rate is accurate enough to justify a claim of IND-CCA2 security [17, 18]. NIST continues to see diversity of computational hardness assumptions as an impor-tant long-term security goal for its standards. NIST will standardize practically efficient schemes from different families of cryptosystems to reduce the risk that a single break-through in cryptanalysis will leave the world without a viable standard for either key-establishment or digital signatures. Nonetheless, NIST does not feel the need to establish these standards all at once but will rather prioritize those schemes that seem closest to be-ing ready for standardization and wide adoption. NIST feels that this strategy balances the desire for diversity with the need for all standards to be thoroughly vetted before they are released.
2.2.2 Cost and Performance

The original call for proposals [9] identified cost as the second most important criterion when evaluating candidate algorithms. Cost includes the computational efficiency of key generation and public and private key operations, the transmission costs for public keys and signatures or ciphertexts, and the implementation costs in terms of RAM (random-access memory) or gate counts. During the third round of the NIST PQC Standardization Process, more information about the computational efficiency of the finalists became available. Faster, constant-time implementations were provided for many of the algorithms (e.g., [19–26]), as were imple-mentations that focused on limiting memory usage (e.g., [27–31]). More information about many of the alternate candidates became available as well. This section focuses on the cost and performance considerations that factored into NIST’s selections. When comparing the overall performance of the algorithms, both computational cost and data transfer cost were considered.2 For general-purpose use, the evaluation of overall performance considered the cost of transferring the public key in addition to the signature or ciphertext during each transaction. For KEMs, the cost of key generation was also taken into account, since many applications use a new KEM key pair for each transaction to pro-vide forward secrecy. For signature algorithms, the cost of key generation was considered less important. At the end of the second round of the NIST PQC Standardization Process, NIST se-lected KYBER, NTRU, and Saber as finalists for the selection of a general-purpose KEM and indicated an intention to select at most one of them [7]. All three have good perfor-mance on both x86-64 processors with AVX2 extensions [33, 34] and the ARM Cortex-M4 [35]. The overall performance of NTRU is not quite as good as KYBER or Saber as a result of its slower key generation and somewhat larger public keys and ciphertexts. How-ever, the overall performance of any of these KEMs would be acceptable for general-use applications. Figure 1 shows the computational performance numbers from [33] for the x86-64 pro-cessor with AVX2 extensions for KYBER, NTRU, and Saber for security categories 1 and 3.3 Figure 2 shows the “total costs” for KYBER, NTRU, and Saber when the cost of data transmission is added. Figure 2 was generated using an estimated cost of 2000 cycles/byte. Encapsulation and decapsulation is very fast with all three schemes. While Saber has the lowest total cost due to its smaller public keys and ciphertexts, the cost difference between KYBER and Saber was not large enough to be considered significant. The cost of key generation for ntruhps2048677 or ntruhrss701 is about 11 times as much as for KYBER512. However, as Figure 2 shows, the total cost for using these schemes tends to be dominated by the cost of data transmission, and so most of the difference in the total cost of the NTRU parameter sets compared to KYBER and Saber is because of NTRU’s somewhat larger public keys and ciphertexts. As a result, the total cost for ntruhps2048677 is less than 30% greater than for KYBER512. In addition, since the public keys and cipher-texts for the category 1 and 3 parameter sets for all three of the schemes are likely to fit within a single internet packet, their performance numbers may be considered comparable. It may also be noted that, according to [33], the cost for key generation for ntruhps2048677 or ntruhrss701 is comparable to the cost of key generation for the elliptic curve cryptogra-phy curve P-256, which is widely used for ephemeral key exchange.4
